description: Static regression expectations for dynamically verified WEB-REAL cases.

cases.deployment_condition: Jersey OAuth1 provider is enabled and request token endpoint is reachable.
cases.notes: Request token strings are retained in DefaultOAuth1Provider.requestTokenByTokenString.

preconditions: Jersey OAuth1 server provider is enabled by the application.
Request-token issuing endpoint is reachable by low-trust clients.
Application accepts enough attacker-controlled token payload or metadata to amplify provider memory.
limiting_factors: OAuth1 server support is optional and not used by most modern Jersey applications.
Authentication, rate limits, or custom token storage can reduce exploitability.
exploitability.rationale: Confirmed real-HTTP heap OOM in the provider path, but only applications that expose Jersey OAuth1 token issuance are in scope.

cases.deployment_condition: Jersey multipart MessageBodyReader is enabled for attacker-controlled multipart requests.
cases.notes: Multipart body parts are accumulated during parser transaction lifetime.

preconditions: Jersey multipart MessageBodyReader is on the classpath and enabled for an upload endpoint.
Low-trust clients can send large multipart bodies with high part count.
Application or front proxy does not enforce tighter request size, part count, or upload quotas.
limiting_factors: Multipart endpoints are application-specific rather than universal.
Reverse proxy/body limits and framework upload limits can block the payload before Jersey parsing.
exploitability.rationale: The parser OOM is realistic for exposed multipart upload endpoints without limits, but not for applications with no multipart entry or strict body quotas.

cases.deployment_condition: Undertow LearningPushHandler is installed in the handler chain.
cases.notes: Outer cache is bounded, but each per-referer inner map can grow by request path.

preconditions: Undertow LearningPushHandler is explicitly installed in the handler chain.
Attacker can send same-referer requests with many unique paths or query strings.
No external path cardinality or per-client request quota is enforced.
limiting_factors: LearningPushHandler is an optional handler, not a default web application path.
Outer referer LRU limits referer count, although the per-referer inner map is unbounded.
exploitability.rationale: Confirmed OOM after installing the optional handler; exploitability depends on that deployment choice.

cases.deployment_condition: MCMP management endpoint is exposed to low-trust clients.
cases.notes: Registry state grows through node, balancer, and virtual host registration.

preconditions: Undertow mod_cluster MCMP management endpoint is deployed.
The management endpoint is reachable by low-trust clients.
The endpoint accepts CONFIG registration requests without an effective auth or network boundary.
limiting_factors: MCMP is a management/control-plane endpoint and should normally be isolated.
Production deployments commonly protect it by network ACLs, management listener separation, or authentication.
exploitability.rationale: The state growth is confirmed, but exposing MCMP management to attackers is an unusual high-risk misconfiguration.

cases.deployment_condition: ProxyServlet deployment maps attacker-controlled request data to HttpClient destination origin or tag.
cases.notes: Harness maps attacker parameter to Jetty Request.tag() for the retained Origin.tag path.

preconditions: Jetty ProxyServlet or equivalent proxy path is deployed.
Attacker-controlled request data can influence HttpClient Origin host, port, scheme, or tag.
Destination idle eviction is disabled or ineffective for the attack duration.
limiting_factors: Many proxy deployments restrict upstream targets or do not map client data into Origin.tag.
Destination idle timeout, allowlists, and upstream normalization can bound the map.
exploitability.rationale: The retained destination map OOM is confirmed in a harness that maps attacker input to Request.tag(); real exploitability depends on comparable proxy rewrite behavior.

cases.deployment_condition: Tomcat WebdavServlet is deployed with WebDAV LOCK enabled and reachable by low-trust clients.
cases.notes: Real HTTP LOCK requests grow resourceLocks and sharedLocks; stable WEB-REAL id covers Phase 4 candidates WEB-P4-0025 through WEB-P4-0027.

preconditions: Tomcat WebdavServlet is deployed and reachable.
WebDAV write methods such as LOCK are enabled for low-trust clients.
No authentication, path quota, or WebDAV-specific rate limit prevents many lock attempts.
limiting_factors: WebDAV writable exposure is uncommon for normal applications and should be protected.
Deployments may disable WebDAV methods or require authentication.
exploitability.rationale: Confirmed with real HTTP LOCK, but the attack requires a writable WebDAV deployment rather than a default ordinary servlet app.

cases.deployment_condition: Tomcat WebdavServlet is deployed with readonly=false, PROPPATCH reachable, and default/unbounded dead-property PropertyStore.
cases.notes: Real HTTP PROPPATCH drove MemoryPropertyStore.deadProperties to heap OOM. Default read-only WebDAV deployments are not exploitable for this path.

preconditions: Tomcat WebdavServlet is deployed and reachable.
The servlet is configured with readonly=false; normal read-only WebDAV mapping is not exploitable for PROPPATCH.
Attacker can create or target existing resources before PROPPATCH.
The default MemoryPropertyStore or another unbounded propertyStore is used for dead properties.
limiting_factors: readonly=false is a non-default editing configuration and normal applications generally should not expose it to untrusted clients.
Custom bounded propertyStore, authentication, or method filtering can block the attack.
exploitability.rationale: Real HTTP heap OOM is confirmed only under writable WebDAV dead-property storage; default read-only deployments should be treated as not exploitable.

cases.deployment_condition: Jetty PushSessionCacheFilter is installed and receives PushBuilder-capable HTTP/2 requests with attacker-controlled paths and same-host Referer.
cases.notes: Real HTTP harness used a PushBuilder-capable wrapper to exercise the filter cache path; static Phase 3 query support is pending.

preconditions: Jetty PushSessionCacheFilter is explicitly installed in the servlet filter chain.
Requests run in a PushBuilder-capable HTTP/2 servlet environment.
Attacker can keep one session and send many unique target/child paths with same-host Referer.
No path cardinality, session size, or global cache quota limits the filter cache.
limiting_factors: PushSessionCacheFilter is optional and HTTP/2 push support is increasingly disabled or unavailable in normal deployments.
Session management, path allowlists, or quotas can bound retention.
exploitability.rationale: Confirmed after wrapping a push-capable request; without the optional filter and PushBuilder-capable environment the vulnerable path is not reached.

cases.deployment_condition: Jetty PushCacheFilter is installed and reachable over HTTP/2 with non-null PushBuilder; attacker controls primary paths and same-host Referer.
cases.notes: Real HTTP harness used a PushBuilder-capable wrapper. _maxAssociations limits children per primary, not primary key cardinality; static Phase 3 query support is pending.

preconditions: Jetty PushCacheFilter is explicitly installed in the servlet filter chain.
Requests use HTTP/2 with request.newPushBuilder() returning a non-null PushBuilder.
Attacker can generate many unique primary paths and same-host Referer associations.
No global primary-resource cache quota or administrative clearPushCache cadence bounds growth.
limiting_factors: The filter short-circuits for HTTP/1.x or null PushBuilder.
_maxAssociations limits children per primary but does not bound the number of primary keys.
The filter is optional and not expected in many current applications.
exploitability.rationale: Confirmed in a push-capable HTTP/2 harness; real exploitability depends on the optional filter being exposed in that environment.

cases.component: Spring Boot 3 HTTP client observation client.name cardinality
cases.deployment_condition: Spring Boot 3 application maps low-trust HTTP input to outbound RestTemplate, RestClient, or WebClient host while Micrometer observation metrics retain http.client.requests client.name tags.
cases.notes: Real HTTP entry drove RestTemplate observation through a local proxy until 384MiB heap OOM. Boot caps the client uri tag by default, but no equivalent default cap was found for client.name.

preconditions: Spring Boot 3 application uses RestTemplate, RestClient, or WebClient with observation metrics enabled.
Low-trust HTTP input controls outbound URL host through an open fetch, proxy, callback, tenant upstream, or equivalent path.
The MeterRegistry retains http.client.requests meters for process lifetime.
No MeterFilter.maximumAllowableTags, host allowlist, egress policy, per-user quota, or client registry eviction bounds outbound host cardinality.
limiting_factors: Spring Boot does not expose an attacker-controlled outbound URL endpoint by default.
Applications with fixed upstream hosts or strict allowlists are not affected by this path.
Custom MeterFilter limits on client.name can bound cardinality before OOM.
exploitability.rationale: Confirmed real-HTTP heap OOM when an application-shaped endpoint maps attacker input to outbound host; exploitability depends on that application path.

cases.deployment_condition: Micronaut application enables in-memory sessions and exposes a low-trust route that creates or saves sessions without max-active-sessions or equivalent quotas.
cases.notes: Real HTTP requests created independent in-memory sessions with attacker-sized attributes until 384MiB heap OOM.

preconditions: Micronaut session module and InMemorySessionStore are enabled.
A low-trust route creates or saves sessions, for example through non-nullable Session binding, @SessionValue, or application session code.
micronaut.session.max-active-sessions is unset or set too high for available heap.
Attacker can create many new sessions and, for strong impact, write non-trivial session attributes within the inactive-expiry window.
limiting_factors: Applications without anonymous session creation paths are not affected by this specific route.
max-active-sessions, per-client quotas, authentication, small attributes, and shorter expiry windows reduce exploitability.
exploitability.rationale: Confirmed real-HTTP heap OOM in the in-memory session store; exploitability depends on an exposed session-creating application route and absent active-session caps.

cases.deployment_condition: Vert.x application uses CachingWebClient in a low-trust request path where attacker input controls outbound cache key and upstream responses are cacheable.
cases.notes: Real HTTP entry mapped attacker query input to CachingWebClient cache keys against a controlled cacheable upstream until 384MiB heap OOM.

preconditions: Application explicitly creates and uses CachingWebClient.
Low-trust HTTP input influences outbound host, path, query, or equivalent CachingWebClient cache key.
Upstream returns cacheable status and cache headers accepted by the Vert.x cache interceptor.
No cache store capacity, byte quota, effective TTL/eviction policy, or per-user quota bounds cache entry cardinality.
limiting_factors: Vert.x does not expose CachingWebClient as a default inbound server endpoint.
Vary caching is disabled by default, limiting one amplification dimension.
Allowlists, fixed upstreams, cache quotas, and non-cacheable upstream responses block or reduce the attack.
exploitability.rationale: Confirmed real-HTTP heap OOM in an application-shaped CachingWebClient path; exploitability is strongest in open fetch/proxy or tenant-upstream patterns.
